neighbours.label: Frames narratives or experiences as first-person or firsthand
fire: The editor describes the novel as a first-person narrative told by a sailor who survives the shipwreck.
The museum pairs each photograph with a first person account written by someone who witnessed the evacuation.
In the foreword, the nurse offers a firsthand account of caring for wounded soldiers during the siege.
The documentary draws on first-hand accounts from residents who remained inside the flooded city.
During the interview, the mechanic described his first-hand experience of repairing engines in Arctic conditions.
The author introduces the book as a first-person memoir of her years working aboard fishing boats.
After returning home, the researcher recorded her first hand experience of daily life in the mountain village.
The publisher calls the diary a firsthand narrative of the expedition, written by its youngest member.
quiet: The review praises the novel's third-person narrative for revealing what several characters believe about the same event.
The biography gives a third-person account of the expedition, pieced together from letters preserved in several distant archives.
The archive preserves secondhand accounts of the strike, compiled by researchers who never visited the factory.
During the workshop, each student rewrote the scene in second person, addressing the reader directly throughout the narrative.
The publisher lists the memoir's page count, binding, price, and release date in the seasonal catalog.
After the witness left, the journalist prepared an account using only a police summary and several unverified rumors.
Although Mara was the first person interviewed, the article contains only the reporter's summary of the meeting.
For her essay on migration, the student analyzed other families' experiences through published statistics and demographic tables.
